alphabet: each piece (7, 9, 11, 15, 17, 19, 21) has its own sign legend, assigned by Bourdeau's transcribers (agent J for 7/9/19/21, agent K for 15, unlisted for 11/17); overlapping short/simple sign names (digits, single Latin letters, a shared descriptive vocabulary for Greek-letter-shaped and geometric signs: LAM, PHI, TRI, DIA, BOX, PLUS...) recur across pieces but are not guaranteed to denote the same underlying cipher sign shape.

constraints.note: token counts are cipher-sign tokens only, from Bourdeau's transcripts, close to but not always identical to his own NOTES.md counts (bracket/punctuation stripping differences of 0-18 tokens per piece).

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Key transfer (this pass, bSIE, 26 Sept 2026): apply Bourdeau's own recovered sign->letter key values for Siena nos. 25, 14 and 4 (his own already-solved siblings in the same busta) against each of the 7 open pieces' own transcripts, literally by sign-name match (case-insensitive fallback). Matched control: the same key applied to the same piece with token order scrambled (3 seeds), which by rule 3/bCAS/AX-5799 must be an ORDER-SENSITIVE statistic since per-token coverage cannot differ under order-scrambling -- used tools/judge_plaintext.py's it-corpus 4-gram score and greedy word-cover on the decoded letters. Cost: this job, $3 cap, Sonnet, no image fetch, no DECODE login. See ciphers/siena-concistoro-2308/NOTES.md for the full 21-cell (7 pieces x 3 keys) table and result.

2. Fallback (not run this pass, queue row 2's own next step): ciphertext-only ic homophonic anneal on nos. 6/24 and 20/23 (~9,000 tokens across the two systems) with a synthetic-Italian control of matching length/design (tools/family_run.py --family homophonic), gated per rule 3 before any target run; a real image fetch and transcription pass would also be needed for pieces 7/9/11/15/17/19/21 themselves if a from-scratch cryptanalysis of any single one is later attempted (Bourdeau's own transcripts are ciphertext-only-unverified against the DECODE images by us).

judge.note: era flag (queue row 2): tools/data/it16 (LANG_CORPORA['it']) is 16th-c. Italian letters, mid-late 16th c. register; these pieces are 15th/early-16th c. (busta spans back to 1421) -- a real era gap, wider than the pt17/es17c precedent (CLAUDE.md rule 3). Graded by eye alongside any score; not trusted on the score alone.

cheap_test_done.method: Bourdeau nos. 25/14/4 key values applied to open pieces 7/9/11/15/17/19/21 (7x3=21 cells), it-corpus score + word-cover, real order vs. 3-seed scrambled-order control (matched per rule 3)
cheap_test_done.result: negative, matched control: every real-order score (-1.56 to -2.45) is below the it corpus's own null_p99 (-1.63 at N=100) or real_p05 (-1.007) in the great majority of cells; real order beats scrambled order in 11/21 cells and loses in 10/21, no consistent one-directional margin, well inside scrambled-control seed noise. None of the three keys decode any of the seven pieces.
